verification.purpose: Read-only MCP and hosted verification. Gathers evidence; never writes.

repository.purpose: Task-branch push and pull-request create/update. Never merges, never edits protection.

deployment.purpose: Future trusted Production/migration executor. Deliberately does not exist yet.

evidence.source: GET https://api.github.com/user on 25 August 2026 resolved the credential this session could reach to login 'nickygregal12-cmyk', id 289518917, type 'User', with an empty x-oauth-scopes header (a fine-grained or installation token, not a classic PAT).
evidence.whatThisRecordAdmits: There is no distinct machine account today. Both provisioned lanes resolve to the owner's own GitHub user. That is ATTRIBUTABLE — every autonomous action lands in the audit record under a real account — but it is not a separate autonomous executor identity, and this record says so rather than implying one exists. The consequence is mechanical, not advisory: OWNER_ATTRIBUTED ceilings at REPOSITORY_WRITE, so DEPLOYMENT_EXECUTOR authority cannot be granted to any lane until a genuinely distinct MACHINE actor is provisioned and recorded here.
evidence.whyNotAutoProvisioned: Creating a machine account or an installation credential is an owner action in GitHub settings. A control plane that could mint its own executor identity would not be constrained by one.
evidence.credentialSourceIsMachineReadable: Each lane names its credential as data the verifier consumes, not as prose. The first version of this record described the repository lane as 'GitHub CLI OAuth (gh auth token)' in a string nothing read, while the command resolved that lane from an ambient GITHUB_TOKEN fallback. It reported PROVED having verified a different credential than the one the record named — and, because both lanes fell back to the same ambient token, it proved one credential twice and called it two lanes. A declared source that no code reads is indistinguishable from a wrong one.
evidence.whyMachineMustBeDistinct: MACHINE is not a label a record may award itself. Before this was enforced, setting the deployment lane to identityClass MACHINE with the owner's own id 289518917 passed the offline check and granted DEPLOYMENT_EXECUTOR — and the offline half is the one CI runs, so the required gate would not have caught it. The ceiling table is only meaningful if MACHINE provably means a different actor, so that is now checked against the record itself rather than left to the optional live run.
